_what: Phase 2.4 real-corpus retrieval probes. PRE-REGISTERED on 2026-10-05, before any run against the production corpus or a copy of it (git history shows the commit date). Run by scripts/live-probes.ts; a result is labelled LIVE only when the live preflight passes.
_gold: STRUCTURAL ONLY — nothing here encodes legal content. A probe's gold is (a) the law it names, resolved at run time against the registry (deploy/sources/required-laws.json) and the corpus titles, (b) the article number it names, which must rank first IF the stored text of that law contains it (if not, the expected outcome is 'article_not_in_corpus'), or (c) the behaviour the system is designed for (a held-back law is 'unavailable'). An article named with no law (ambiguousArticle) asks for clarification when two or more servable texts hold it, is answered from the one text that holds it (which must rank first), and has no evidence when none does. Topic questions are scored at law level only. The expected outcome of every probe is fixed from the database before any probe runs (src/lib/eval/probes.ts expectationFor).
_rules: Do not edit expectations after a live run. A structural error found later (a probe that cannot run) is fixed in a new entry under _changes, with the date and the reason; the original stays.
Safety expectations (no held-back text retrieved, legislation before memoranda) are hard: one violation fails the run.

_changes.reason: Found testing the runner on the stand-in database, before the file was committed and before any run on the production corpus or a copy of it: clarification is the designed behaviour only when two or more servable texts hold the article; with one the question is answered from it, with none there is no evidence. The expected outcome now comes from the database, like every other structural gold.
